title: DBMUXEv v0.2
description: Bundle of all DBMUXEv document schemas. Each document type is under #/definitions/<type>. YAML integer keys (eg. value tables written as 0x01:) are validated after conversion to JSON, where they become decimal strings.

identifier.description: Unique names/IDs: english, uppercase, digits and underscores only

node_name.description: Node (ECU) name, as defined in nodes/<arch>.<variant>.yml

lang_code.description: ISO 639-1 language code, optionally with a region (eg. zh, pt-BR)

multilang.description: Translated text. 'en' is mandatory, 'fr' is strongly recommended (validator warning). Other supported languages: es, de, it, pl, ru, zh, hu, pt (any ISO 639-1 code is accepted).

hex_or_int.description: An integer. In YAML, write it as hex (0x1A) or decimal

bits.description: Bit position in PSA notation <byte>.<bit>, bytes are numbered from 1 (first transmitted byte), bits from 7 (MSB, first transmitted) to 0. A range is <start>-<end> in transmission order (big-endian / Motorola), eg. '1.7-2.0' is a 16 bit value spanning bytes 1 and 2. For variable length (can-tp / diag) payloads, the end can be 'n' (until the end of the payload), eg. '3.7-n'

periodicity.description: How the frame is sent: a list of periods ('100ms') and/or 'trigger' (sent on event/change). A frame both periodic and sent on change is ['100ms', 'trigger']. A frame only sent on request (VAN reply, diag) is 'request'.

value_entry.description: Meaning of one raw value. Either a translated text (multilang), optionally flagged 'unused' (reserved/never observed), or only {unused: true}

value_table.description: Raw value (hex 0x.. or decimal integer key) to meaning. Never write binary-looking keys like 010, YAML reads them as decimal

signal.description: A value carried inside a frame (or inside a diag payload)

unused.description: Reserved / always observed at the same value / padding

type.description: uint (default): unsigned integer; sint: two's complement signed integer; bool: 1 bit flag; enum: integer whose meaning is given by 'values'; bcd: binary coded decimal; str: text (ASCII/ISO-8859-1); bytes: opaque raw bytes; float: IEEE754. Legacy types (uint8, uint16, uint24, int8, int16, int24) are accepted but deprecated.

default.description: Raw value sent when the data is not (yet) available, eg. at wakeup

mux_selector.description: This signal selects which multiplexed signals are present in the frame

mux.description: This signal is only present when the selector signal has one of these raw values

alternatives.description: Conflicting observations for this signal: each item overrides some fields of the signal. Kept so maintainers can decide which one is right

receivers.description: When only some of the frame receivers use this signal

byte_order.description: Byte order of a multi-byte value. PSA uses big endian (most significant byte first) almost everywhere; 'little_endian' means the covered bytes are sent least significant byte first ('bits' still gives the covered range in transmission order)

message.description: One frame on a bus (CAN, CAN-TP/ISO-TP, VAN or LIN). File: buses/<arch>.<variant>/<network>.<bus>/<ID>.yml (optionally <ID>_<SUFFIX>.yml when several frames share an ID)

length.description: Payload length in bytes (maximum length for can-tp)

length_min.description: Shortest length accepted/observed, when receivers accept shorter frames

observations.description: Free notes about how the frame behaves on the bus

alternatives.description: Conflicting observations for the whole frame (other length, period, senders, or other signal layout). Each item overrides the given fields; 'signals' here fully replaces the signal map. Kept so maintainers can decide which one is right

isotp.description: ISO 15765-2 (ISO-TP / CAN-TP) transport. The frame 'id' is the CAN ID carrying the data (sender side); signals describe the reassembled payload (byte 1 = first payload byte after the PCI)

flow_control_id.description: CAN ID used by the receiver for flow control frames

address.description: First byte of the frame for extended/mixed addressing

padding.description: Padding byte used to fill frames to 8 bytes, or null when frames are not padded (DLC < 8)

van.description: VAN (ISO 11519-3) specifics. The frame 'id' is the 12 bit identifier. The 4 bit command field is EXT (always 1), RAK (acknowledge request), R/W and RTR

access.description: write: the producer sends its data (R/W=0). read: the frame is a read request answered by the producer (R/W=1). read-write: both are observed

ack.description: RAK bit: an in-frame acknowledge is requested

reply.description: For read requests: in-frame (the producer fills the data field of the request frame itself) or deferred (the producer answers later with a separate frame)

requested_by.description: Nodes that issue the read request

lin.description: LIN specifics. 'id' is the 6 bit frame identifier (0x00-0x3F)

protected_id.description: Identifier with parity bits, as seen on the wire

master.description: LIN master of the bus (header sender)

parent.description: Variant this one derives from (frames not redefined are the same)

id.description: Electronic unit code per network (used in supervision/version/wakeup frames and diag addressing)

released.description: false for nodes that never reached a production car

node_diag.description: Short diag addressing summary (full details in diag/)

codes.description: Subset of codes this version applies to (default: all)

nodes.description: Nodes (ECUs) seen in this version, per network. Mandatory nodes are always fitted, optional ones depend on trim/options

optional_nodes.description: Nodes of the 'nodes' map that are only fitted with some options/trims

buses.description: Buses of the architecture fitted on this version (<network>.<bus>); some only come with optional nodes

ecu_models.description: ECU models seen on this version, per node (as in diag/<arch>/<node>/<model>/)

diag_ecu.description: diag/<arch>.<variant>/<NODE>/ecu.yml: how to talk to one ECU

bus.description: <network>.<bus> the tester is connected to (usually through the diag socket / gateway)

services.description: Supported service IDs (0x10, 0x22...), see diag/protocols/<protocol>.yml for their definition

algorithm.description: Name of the seed/key algorithm (see diag/protocols)

key.description: ECU specific constant fed to the algorithm

model.description: ECU model (hardware / software family), when the node has several models: diag/<arch>.<variant>/<NODE>/<MODEL>/

identification.description: How to read the ECU part number, which gives the software variant

part_number.description: Position of the part number in the answer data (after the service and identifier bytes)

cars.description: Cars (cars/<project>.yml) this ECU model was seen on

variants.description: Software variants of this ECU model: variant id -> part numbers and cars

diag_data.description: diag/<arch>.<variant>/<NODE>/dids/<DID>.yml (UDS ReadDataByIdentifier 0x22 / WriteDataByIdentifier 0x2E) or lids/<LID>.yml (KWP2000 ReadDataByLocalIdentifier 0x21 / WriteDataByLocalIdentifier 0x3B)

kind.description: live: measured value; config: coding / configuration (usually writable); identification: part numbers, versions

security_level.description: Security access level needed to write it

length.description: Payload length in bytes (without the service/identifier bytes), null when variable

variants.description: ECU sub-families this identifier was seen on

service.description: Service used to read it, when not the usual one (eg. 0x1A ReadEcuIdentification for files named <ID>_IDENT.yml)

variants.description: ECU software variants (see the variants of ecu.yml) this applies to

length.description: Payload length in bytes (without the service/identifier bytes), null when variable

alternatives.description: Other layouts (other software variants, or other readings of the same bytes); params replaces the whole params map

diag_dtcs.description: diag/<arch>.<variant>/<NODE>/dtcs.yml: DTC code (P/C/B/U + 4 hex, optionally -XX failure type) -> description

raw.description: Code as sent on the bus (hex)

failure_types.description: Failure type (characterisation) byte sent with 2 byte codes

variants.description: ECU software variants (see the variants of ecu.yml) this applies to

controls.description: Control option values (UDS: first data byte, 00 return control, 03 short term adjustment...)

variants.description: ECU software variants (see the variants of ecu.yml) this applies to

diag_protocol.description: diag/protocols/<PROTOCOL>.yml: generic definition of a diagnostic protocol (services, sub-functions, negative response codes)

diag_test.description: Actuator test using this routine / io control, as offered by diagnostic tools

mapped_signal.description: A value of a mapped identifier: same as a signal, but its position is given by the ECU parameter table (index) instead of bits

unused.description: Reserved / always observed at the same value / padding

type.description: uint (default): unsigned integer; sint: two's complement signed integer; bool: 1 bit flag; enum: integer whose meaning is given by 'values'; bcd: binary coded decimal; str: text (ASCII/ISO-8859-1); bytes: opaque raw bytes; float: IEEE754. Legacy types (uint8, uint16, uint24, int8, int16, int24) are accepted but deprecated.

default.description: Raw value sent when the data is not (yet) available, eg. at wakeup

mux_selector.description: This signal selects which multiplexed signals are present in the frame

mux.description: This signal is only present when the selector signal has one of these raw values

alternatives.description: Conflicting observations for this signal: each item overrides some fields of the signal. Kept so maintainers can decide which one is right

receivers.description: When only some of the frame receivers use this signal

byte_order.description: Byte order of a multi-byte value. PSA uses big endian (most significant byte first) almost everywhere; 'little_endian' means the covered bytes are sent least significant byte first ('bits' still gives the covered range in transmission order)

index.description: Index of the value in the ECU parameter table

diag_mapped.description: Values without fixed position (the ECU sends the layout itself)
